races.name: Schweppes Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Two Tribes
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with two wins and five placings from twelve races on similar going; Saffie Osborne fits well, and the step up from 6f to 7f suits, though OR 103 makes this the stiffest task he has faced in this grade.

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who knows his job from a prominent pitch, with an outstanding record of fourteen placings in fifteen good-ground starts; Lewis Edmunds is a light-weight booking and 35 days off is within his normal pattern, but his sole win came on good and the 97 OR is competitive.

runners_data.name: Addison Grey
runners_data.note: Three wins from eleven on similar going is a strong conversion rate; Callum Shepherd has ridden him to good effect before, the 7f at Ascot is a slight stretch from his favoured 6f, but his latest win over this trip shows he stays.

runners_data.name: Lord Britain
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse who needs the race to be run at a strong pace to be delivered late; De Sousa is the booking of note, but only four qualifying runs from nine on good or similar ground is a concern, and his best form has come on faster surfaces.

runners_data.name: Ghost Mode
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters; won over 7f on good ground at this course last time, so the combination of track, trip, and going is proven — the danger is that Mubasimah, from the same stable, will fight him for the lead and drain his stamina.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: The second Balding front-runner, whose most recent form has come on soft ground with limited good-ground evidence (six runs on similar going, one win two places); the internal yard battle for the lead with Ghost Mode is the defining tactical question, and if she concedes it early she has limited other gears.

runners_data.name: The Fingal Raven
runners_data.note: Comes in with strong recent good-ground form including a third over this course and trip last time; naturally wants to race prominently but with six prominent-minded horses ahead of him in the map, he will find himself further back than ideal — his 0.93 style-fit reflects the compromise, and his chance depends on the race opening up late.

runners_data.name: Silver Ghost
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer with fifteen qualifying runs on similar going (two wins, seven places), making her one of the most consistent course-profile fits in the field; the concern is she recorded a 15th and 10th in her last two outings on this track, and Emma Lavelle's stable is currently out of form (0 from 7 over 14 days).

runners_data.name: Thunder Call
runners_data.note: Won his last two starts (6f, good and standard) and is improving; the step to 7f at Ascot is the unknown — all five recent runs have been at six furlongs — but his Haggas training and Cieren Fallon partnership add significant confidence, and the prominent style suits a race where at least some pace will be set.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground recently and has multiple placings at the trip; a natural prominent racer who the congestion will push into a midfield role he has not had to race from — his style-fit score reflects that compromise, and Edward Greatrex will need a clean passage that the traffic scenario makes unlikely.

races.paceDynamic: Ghost Mode and Mubasimah are the two confirmed front-runners trained by the same yard (Andrew Balding), and their direct clash from the gates will set a genuine, contested gallop over Ascot's straight seven furlongs — neither is likely to surrender without a fight, meaning the pace will be honest from the off. Behind them, Two Tribes, Northern Express, Addison Grey, and Thunder Call all want prominent positions, creating a wall of horses across the opening two furlongs and a real squeeze for space around the 2-3 furlong marker where the field begins to stack up. This field contains more prominent types than the track can accommodate — The Fingal Raven and Glenfinnan are both natural prominent racers who will be shuffled into midfield roles they did not choose, compromising their ability to travel in their preferred position. The contested early fractions on good ground at a stiff seven furlongs favour horses who can settle mid-to-rear and produce one sustained run into the straight — hold-up horses and those with proven ability to finish strongly off a genuine pace will be best placed, while those in the prominent scrum risk getting involved in early attrition they cannot recover from.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Strong Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Mode and Mubasimah fight for the front and the honest gallop stretches the prominent group, setting up the straight for finishers.
scenarios.body: The two Balding leaders burn each other and the prominent pack into a strong pace, leaving the straight open for those who have been restrained; good ground at Ascot rewards the horse that picks up late with a clean run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Ghost Mode (or Mubasimah) establishes a clear lead early and the pace settles into a controlled but honest gallop.
scenarios.body: A single pace-setter controlling from the front means the prominent racers behind can travel comfortably and pounce without burning stamina fighting for position; Two Tribes and Thunder Call, both with good prominent records on good ground, are ideally suited.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders cancel each other out early and the pace drops to a crawl, bunching the field and producing a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow-burn race plays into the hands of the prominent types who have held a good position throughout without burning energy; Addison Grey's three wins in twelve on similar going and Thunder Call's strong tactical speed make them obvious beneficiaries of a compact dash to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion between the prominent group produces interference at the 2-3 furlong marker, disrupting multiple horses and randomising the finish.
scenarios.body: The wall of prominent runners collides as they try to quicken simultaneously, causing switches and checks that open the door for a horse that has been given the cleanest passage; Silver Ghost and Lord Britain, sitting further back with clear sightlines, are the beneficiaries if the gaps open late.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a fierce duel between Ghost Mode and Mubasimah in the first two furlongs — if both Balding horses lock horns at the head of affairs, the pace could be severely overdone and neither may finish, exposing those in the prominent group.

The 2-3 furlong marker is a congestion flashpoint — with Two Tribes, Northern Express, Addison Grey, and Thunder Call all pressing for the same prominent ground behind the leaders, interference or a check is a real risk that could derail multiple fancied runners simultaneously.

The Fingal Raven and Glenfinnan are both likely to find themselves racing out of their natural prominent role; if either gets pocketed behind the prominent wall they lack the hold-up finishing kick to compensate, and their chances hinge entirely on getting a clear run earlier than their redistributed position suggests.

Silver Ghost's last two efforts at Ascot were poor (15th and 10th) despite the strong course-going profile — watch for whether she travels with her usual fluency from the gate, as a flat-track bullying profile may not suit her if the field fans across the wide straight.

Thunder Call has never run beyond 6f — his prominent, front-foot style should help him conserve energy through the first half, but watch how he responds when the pace quickens off the turn, as the extra furlong at Ascot's stiff straight is an unproven stamina test for this horse.

races.name: TOTE.CO.UK Money Back 2nd Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Archers Bay
runners_data.note: Botti-trained 3yo with a win over 12f on Good ground, wears headgear and has Place form on similar going (4/9 across good-ground runs); races prominently and will need to avoid the congestion among the prominent group in what is a traffic-heavy shape, but the step up to 1m4f at Ascot suits a horse with a recent win at 12f.

runners_data.name: Guildmaster
runners_data.note: Gosden yard, 79 days off the track which is a flag in a competitive heritage handicap; produced solid form at 10f on Good ground and the step to 1m4f is unexplored, with the question of whether he truly gets the trip the key unknown — Robert Havlin takes the ride for one of the stronger yards in training.

runners_data.name: Into The Light
runners_data.note: Appleby runner who won last time over 11f on Good, has the strongest recent form profile in the race; Toby Moore takes a 7lb claim which effectively drops him to a very competitive weight, and while he showed in his last win he can handle Good ground, a distant 15th on Soft last time over 14f is a distance query worth noting.

runners_data.name: Decade Of Time
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Jack Channon who will go straight to the front from stall; has won twice and placed five times in nine career starts, but all his good form has come over 8-10f and the jump to 1m4f on a track as demanding as Ascot is an unresolved stamina question — George Bass rides.

runners_data.name: Ancestor
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained 3yo with two wins from three career starts, both at 10f on Good ground; he is a confirmed front-runner who has shown a willingness to compete freely, and Cieren Fallon gives him a high-class pilot, but the Haggas yard is in exceptional form (11/52 T14) and the step to 1m4f is the only open question for a horse with a clean record.

runners_data.name: Heyzoom
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows 3yo who is by nature a prominent racer — placed in his map to midfield only because the field cannot accommodate the number of horses that want to race there; a genuine 90-day absence is a fitness concern, and while his form on similar going is solid, the style displacement means he may not get the position that brings out his best.

runners_data.name: Turty Tree
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding runner who wears headgear and has won over 10f on Good ground, recently second over 11f on Good; races prominently and has consistent Place form across good ground (5/7 sim-going strikes), and the extra distance to 1m4f looks within his compass given his record — David Probert is an able partner.

runners_data.name: Cape Fear
runners_data.note: Balding 3yo with an excellent record on Good ground — 9/9 similar-going runs with two wins and eight places, and wins at 12f; by nature a prominent performer, he is shown at the rear only because the field is congested with pace and a less pace-committed prominent horse is mapped back — Jason Watson must work out how to find cover without being too far back for his natural finishing position.

runners_data.name: Lord d'Or
runners_data.note: Nicola Currie rides for Balding, a confirmed front-runner who has finished second in four of his last five career starts, suggesting a horse that places well but cannot win from the front — an honest galloper who will be squeezed by Decade Of Time and Ancestor for early supremacy and is likely to find three front-runners going too many in a 1m4f heritage handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Decade Of Time, Ancestor, and Lord d'Or are all confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner field over 1m4f on Good ground at Ascot, making a strong, contested gallop virtually inevitable from the outset. With three genuine leaders vying for the same piece of real estate down the back straight, the pace will be honest to fast, and the stamina demands will be relentless through Ascot's punishing straight. Archers Bay, Guildmaster, Into The Light, Turty Tree, and Heyzoom all want to race prominently, meaning the race will be strung out early with significant positional congestion between two and three furlongs out. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions — Decade Of Time and Ancestor are best placed to actually dictate given their confirmed lead profiles, with Lord d'Or likely pressured into a harder race than ideal. This race shape decisively favours genuine stamina types that can travel through a true pace from midfield and sustain their effort up the straight — horses racing prominently off a hot early gallop will be exposed, and those with the ability to settle and finish strongly are best suited.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Stayers Triumph
scenarios.trigger: If Decade Of Time, Ancestor, and Lord d'Or force a genuine end-to-end gallop that burns off the prominent pack
scenarios.body: The three leaders create a searching pace that strings the field out, leaving those who have raced freely too exposed in the final two furlongs of Ascot's straight; horses who have settled in midfield and possess confirmed stamina over this trip can absorb the pace and reel in the leaders late

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Escapes Modest Hold
scenarios.trigger: If one leader — most likely Ancestor or Decade Of Time — gets a split second of comfort at the front and builds an unassailable lead before the home turn
scenarios.body: Rather than a truly brutal pace war, one front-runner dictates at a strong but measured tempo, using Ascot's long straight to grind rivals flat before they can mount a challenge; the winner will be a front-runner whose stamina and jumping ability at Ascot's unique track profile allows them to sustain the effort all the way to the line

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace, while honest, does not fully brutalize the leaders and the race is run at a tempo that suits horses just off the pace
scenarios.body: Archers Bay or Guildmaster, tracking the leaders in a prominent position and never having to expend energy in a positional battle, find a smooth passage at the top of the straight and sustain their effort to the line; this scenario is less likely given the density of prominent runners creating traffic and congestion two to three furlongs out

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so savage that it creates a truly dramatic late collapse and the race sets up for hold-up horses
scenarios.body: Cape Fear, though a natural prominent type redistributed to the rear, would need to overcome an out-of-role position and is not a true hold-up performer; this scenario is markedly discounted because there are no genuine hold-up horses in this field — those mapped to the rear are prominent types by nature and unlikely to deliver in a shape that demands a true hold-up performance

watchPoints.text: Positional battle between Decade Of Time, Ancestor, and Lord d'Or in the first two furlongs is the defining moment of this race — whichever of the three is forced to race wider or harder than intended early will have their stamina compromised by the finish.

Archers Bay, Guildmaster, Into The Light, Turty Tree, and Heyzoom all want to be prominent — watch for significant crowding and checking two to three furlongs out as the tightly grouped prominent pack meets the wall of leaders under pressure.

Heyzoom's 79-day absence combined with being forced out of his natural prominent position is a dual concern — Owen Burrows runners can return fresh but the style displacement compounds the fitness risk in a race that will be run at a true pace.

Into The Light's Toby Moore 7lb claim is a significant positive on paper, but watch the draw and whether a 3yo with a distant 15th on Soft over 14f can handle Ascot's unique stamina demands at this distance when the pace is genuinely hot.

Cape Fear's exceptional record on Good ground (9/9) is the most striking stat in the race and worth monitoring — if the race truly falls apart up front, his Good-ground class gives him a latent finishing chance even from a position further back than his natural style would prefer.

races.name: tote £75k Guaranteed Placepot Today EBF "Confined" Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses Which Have Run No More Than Once) (GBB Race)
Silent Pool Gin "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Won No More Than One Race)

runners_data.name: Gavriel
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's 3yo has won on equivalent good-to-firm turf and showed class when second at a similar trip; a prominent style suits this Ascot straight and Robert Havlin rides from a solid recent platform with the stable in fair 14-day form at 6/18.|

runners_data.name: Balzac
runners_data.note: Finished third twice over this distance on good ground and has the stamina profile to benefit if the pace is truly strong; Sorin Moldoveanu's 7lb claim helps on the weights, though 77 days off and a genuine hold-up style means Balzac needs the front to have run themselves into the ground.|

runners_data.name: Lion of Alba
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets the terms and races in a tongue-tie; his Good-ground record over this trip reads 6/7 sim-going and he has been beaten at odds-on recently, so the question is whether his front-running courage is enough to hold a quality prominent group — David Probert will need to judge the fractions shrewdly.|

runners_data.name: Law Court
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's consistent 3yo has placed five times on good ground and won once, making him exactly the profile that benefits from a controlled lead to chase; Faleh Bughanaim takes over the ride for a trainer whose 14-day strike rate (0/45) tempers enthusiasm, but the horse's own form is the most reliable in the field.|

runners_data.name: Dark Whisper
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 3yo won over 8f on good ground and placed at 8f and 10f on the same surface — the step up to 10f looks a natural fit; Saffie Osborne's claim brings the weight down and the horse's 4/4 sim-going record is the strongest striking rate in this field, though the drop to an OR of 85 suggests the stable is hunting a winnable spot.|

runners_data.name: Now Maybe
runners_data.note: George Baker's 3yo has placed twice over longer trips on good ground and is genuinely a prominent-style horse; with Lion of Alba, Gavriel, Law Court, and Dark Whisper all seeking similar early real estate, Now Maybe is likely to find that ground taken and will need to settle for a position further back than suits — style-fit of 0.94 signals its chance is tempered in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Kahin
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends out this 3yo who won over 9f on good ground and has placed twice at 10f, so the trip and going are squarely in his favour; wearing a hood (headgear: p) may aid concentration, but he's naturally a horse that wants to race close to the pace and the congested prominent tier means he is likely pushed wider or further back than Haggas would prefer — his chance depends partly on how well he adapts.|

races.paceDynamic: Lion of Alba is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on a clear lead with David Probert aboard, will dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this mile-and-two on good ground at Ascot — not a suicidal pace, but enough to test those who try to match him early. Gavriel, Law Court, and Dark Whisper are all prominent types who will queue up behind, creating a compact early order but without the horse-for-horse battle that would burn Lion of Alba off. The redistribution flags on Now Maybe and Kahin are significant: both are natural prominent racers who will find that position already congested, and Kahin (headgear: p) in particular will need to adapt to a midfield role that is not his instinct. This race shape — a lone, unchallenged pace-setter over a stamina-testing ten furlongs on good turf — materially favours prominent horses with a strong cruising speed who can sit just off the leader and pounce in the straight, rather than genuine hold-up types who must produce a sustained finish from further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Lion of Alba is allowed to stride clear and set a measured, uncontested gallop throughout, the prominent horses directly behind inherit the ideal stalking position.
scenarios.body: Lion of Alba rolls along at a fair but manageable tempo, and the best-placed prominent type — nestled just off his shoulder — takes over two furlongs out without ever having been asked a serious question through the race; the sustained run into the Ascot straight rewards a horse with tactical speed and class rather than raw stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is fractionally steadier than expected and a prominent runner times a decisive mid-race move to sprint clear before the field can organise.
scenarios.body: A modest early tempo compresses the field, and the horse with the best turn of foot from a prominent position exploits the momentary hesitation to steal a march two furlongs out; Ascot's straight rewards those who kick first and sustain it.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast, Pace Fades
scenarios.trigger: If Lion of Alba's front-running effort, combined with an uncommonly strong gallop from the prominent group, sets a pace hot enough to burn off the mid-division and collapse the front two late.
scenarios.body: The field fans wide in the straight and horses that have been conserved deepest — notably Balzac, who has the form and stamina profile for exactly this scenario — come through strongest; Kahin, though racing out of his natural role, could also emerge if pace collapse is severe enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Prominent Jam Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent glut causes crowding early and several prominent types end up shuffled back, scrambling the predicted order.
scenarios.body: Now Maybe and Kahin, both frustrated out of their natural positions, race with more intent than the map suggests and disrupt the pace pattern entirely, producing a scrambled finish where the horse with the widest draw or clearest passage benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Lion of Alba's pace judgment is the fulcrum of the entire race — if David Probert misjudges and either sprints too fast early or dawdles enough to invite a prominent horse to take over cheaply, the race shape changes entirely.

The prominent cluster of Law Court, Gavriel, and Dark Whisper all seeking the same ground two or three off the leader could produce early jostling; any horse squeezed or checked in that group loses the tactical advantage the scenario is built around.

Kahin (hood, William Haggas) is 57 days off the track and races in a style that the current field shape denies him — monitor whether he settles at the back of the prominent bunch or fights for position and expends energy unnecessarily in the first half-mile.

Balzac's 77-day absence and hold-up style means he is the most dependent on a strong gallop; if Lion of Alba produces only a moderate tempo, Balzac's finishing run from the rear simply will not be sufficient on a track that typically rewards position over raw closing speed.

Dark Whisper's 4/4 record on similar going is the cleanest surface stat in the race and warrants tracking through the early stages — if Saffie Osborne gets a clean, prominent position with a clear view to challenge, the horse's course-relevant profile makes it a live threat in the straight.

races.name: Download The Tote App British Ebf Premier Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Nanino Niyati
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner for Owen Burrows, fresh off a win at 10f on good but a return to 8f raises questions about whether she can lead fast enough to be competitive; 39 days off the track is manageable and David Probert rides, but three rivals will challenge her for the lead from the gate and that early battle is the primary risk.

runners_data.name: Seren Star
runners_data.note: William Haggas's hold-up filly has a strong record at 8f on good going (won at Chepstow at the trip), and Cieren Fallon gives her a classic hold-up ride in what should be a strongly-run race; headgear flagged, and 27 days since last run is fine, but a wide draw or traffic in the straight could prove costly.

runners_data.name: Orion's Belt
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 3yo is on a losing run of five with the best recent effort being an 11th and a 10th, both on soft; Pat Dobbs keeps the ride but stepping back up to 8f on good ground after three poor efforts is hard to support without a clear form uptick.

runners_data.name: Tryst
runners_data.note: George Boughey's filly has won back-to-back at 7f on good ground (Good to Firm) and now steps up to a mile in a handicap; headgear worn previously and Jack Callan partners her — the hold-up style suits this pace scenario perfectly, but the distance extension to 8f is the key question mark after her two wins over seven.

runners_data.name: Rosa Inglesa
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes's 3yo is prominent by style but without the same kamikaze front-running agenda as the trio at the head of the market; Lewis Edmunds takes over and she has a solid record at 8f on good going (two wins), making her a logical beneficiary if she can slot cleanly into second gear off the fierce early pace.

runners_data.name: True Test
runners_data.note: William Knight's 3yo has a busy trainer (5 wins from 12 in 14 days) and Neil Callan takes the ride; a best recent run of 2nd at 8f good going suggests latent ability, but a record of 4-2-0-6-3-7 over varying trips on good ground is too patchy to inspire confidence in this competitive heat.

runners_data.name: Luna Celeste
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's progressive filly has three wins at 8f on good going and a fourth at 6f — a consistent profile ideally suited to a flat Ascot mile; Saffie Osborne rides and 20 days since last win is sharp, with a trainer in form (4/15) and a genuinely well-matched distance and going combination.

runners_data.name: Electrifarhh
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 4yo has a prominent running style and a respectable trainer strike-rate but no wins in the last five; the best recent effort was a 2nd at 8f on good going, yet the form has softened and George Downing comes in for the ride — a difficult profile to get enthused about in this company.

runners_data.name: Date Line
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's lightly-raced 3yo has run just three times, winning at 7f and placing in both other starts, all on good ground; Callum Shepherd partners her and at OR 85 she is the lightest-burdened of the front-runners, which may help her secure a comfortable lead if Nanino Niyati and Applesandpears are slow away — the key watch for any tactical vacuum.

runners_data.name: Applesandpears
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 3yo wants to lead but arrives 50 days off the track with a form line that includes a win at 6f on standard and four runs without a victory since; Silvestre De Sousa is a major booking upgrade and headgear flagged, but declining OR 83 and the fact she must fight two other confirmed front-runners for the lead makes this a complicated profile.

races.paceDynamic: Nanino Niyati, Date Line and Applesandpears all want to lead, creating a genuine three-way battle for the front that will inject early tempo into this flat Ascot mile — a strong gallop is virtually guaranteed from the outset. Rosa Inglesa, True Test and Luna Celeste will look to press them into a prominent position, meaning the front half of the field is congested and runners will be jostling for space around the bend 2-3 furlongs out. That pace will be maintained into the straight, compressing the finish and ensuring the race is run at a punishing, honest clip throughout — stamina and the ability to sustain an effort will be at a premium. This race shape emphatically favours hold-up horses or those able to travel smoothly just off the pace, as the front-running trio will have burned each other's petrol; Seren Star, Tryst and Orion's Belt are ideally positioned to capitalise if they get a clear run in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, closers strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle burns out the leaders early, the hold-up and back-section runners come into their own turning for home.
scenarios.body: Nanino Niyati, Date Line and Applesandpears wage war up front and tie each other up, leaving the field strung out at halfway with the pace collapsing as they hit the two-furlong marker; those settled behind the carnage come with a sweeping run. Seren Star (William Haggas, good-ground record) and Tryst (back-to-back wins at 7f on good, now stepping into a truly-run mile) are perfectly suited, able to pick off the tiring pace horses late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent racer outstays field
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent runner tracks the pace without burning excess energy and finds the gaps at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Rosa Inglesa and Luna Celeste sit just off the speed and are gifted a slingshot as the true pace horses weaken — both have strong records at a mile on good ground and profile as likely beneficiaries of a strongly-run race without being directly involved in the early scrapping. Luna Celeste's three wins at 8f on good going and sharp recent form make her particularly well-placed to sustain the gallop through the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front runner survives chaos
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters breaks cleanly, takes a clear lead and is allowed to dictate at a controlled rather than suicidal tempo.
scenarios.body: Date Line is most likely to benefit here — lightly raced with three career runs, all at the current trip, and a clean record of 1-2-2 on good going, she is less battle-hardened than Nanino Niyati and Applesandpears and could exploit any tactical vacuum if those rivals fail to go with her immediately. The mile on a flat, fair Ascot track over Good ground plays to a front-runner's strengths if the pace is measured rather than contested.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up from deep, stamina test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly searching and the field strings out, allowing a deep hold-up runner to make late ground past exhausted rivals.
scenarios.body: Orion's Belt has a disappointing recent run of form (10-11-9 in last three) and a concerning profile stepping up from 6-7f, but in a truly extreme stamina test could in theory be delivered very late by Pat Dobbs; however the lack of any recent win and deteriorating form makes this a low-probability hope. Electrifarhh, too prominent-natured to truly benefit from this scenario, offers limited upside.

watchPoints.text: Watch Nanino Niyati, Date Line and Applesandpears in the first two furlongs — if all three go for the lead simultaneously the resulting pace will be severe and any runner caught in that early bunching faces a rough, energy-sapping journey.

Luna Celeste's position rounding the turn is critical — with four horses fighting for prominent slots, traffic between the two-furlong marker and the home bend is likely and any slight interference could cost her a decisive length.

Date Line is the one front-runner to watch if she breaks cleanly and the others are slow to react — a lightly-raced filly with a clean slate on good going at this trip could steal a march on the field if left alone in front.

Seren Star's late run depends entirely on a clear passage in the straight; Ascot's wide mile track helps, but in a field of 10 with a congested mid-section, Cieren Fallon will need to time his run precisely from the back.

Tryst's stamina for the mile is the horse to monitor through the final furlong — her two wins came at 7f and if she runs out of gallop in the closing stages a prominent finishing position in a strong-pace race tells little about future trips.

races.name: Club26 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ferrous
runners_data.note: Consistent 6f hold-up performer on Good ground but OR 99 suggests a tough mark, and six-year-old yet to win this season; sim-going record of just 2 places from 4 offers limited encouragement on a track where closers need clean air|

runners_data.name: Golden Mind
runners_data.note: Fahey yard in decent 14-day form (9/63) but this horse's recent runs are all on 7f or Soft, with no wins and no places in 8 sim-going attempts at 6f on Good — significant concern despite Oisin Orr's booking|

runners_data.name: Garfield Shadow

races.paceDynamic: Havana Blue is the sole confirmed front runner and should lead comfortably from stall, setting a genuine but sustainable gallop on Good ground over 6f at Ascot — a course that rewards horses who can hold a prominent position without being overhauled. With no serious challenger for the lead, Havana Blue can dictate a controlled tempo, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which typically compresses the field and makes it harder for deep hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need late. The prominent brigade — Garfield Shadow, Mirabeau, Fast Track Harry, American Gulf, and Golden Long — are best placed to track the steady pace and pounce, while the numerous hold-up horses face the genuine risk of never getting into the race on a track where cover and early position matter enormously. This field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; Diligently, Sword, Saint Lawrence, Fifty Nifty, and Northcliff are all true closers who are unlikely to secure their natural position, with Golden Long and Garfield Shadow the most likely to actually land prominent ground. The dominant profile favoured here is the prominent racer who can sit just off a controlled Havana Blue and unleash a sustained finish in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Havana Blue Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Blue dictates an uncontested, comfortable tempo and the prominent trackers pounce in the straight
scenarios.body: Havana Blue controls the race from the front at a measured pace, leaving her rivals to battle for position behind while the field compresses into the final two furlongs; horses like Garfield Shadow, Golden Long, and Fast Track Harry, who can settle just off the pace, are ideally placed to launch sustained challenges

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Havana Blue Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Havana Blue is never seriously pressured and finds extra in the final furlong to hold on
scenarios.body: With no challenger pushing Havana Blue for the lead, she is able to regulate her own fractions and conserve enough energy to repel rivals late; at OR 85 with recent good-ground winning form and a positive recent run, she remains a live chance to simply steal the race from the front

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and genuine hold-up runners get a clear run to close into a tiring field
scenarios.body: Should the pace quicken materially in the middle stages, or jostling in a 15-runner field creates late gaps, true hold-up types who secure a clean passage could finish with purpose; Diligently — the best-credentialled of the redistributed closers with a superior sim-going record — and Havana Hurricane are best placed to exploit any such gap

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Movers Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 15-runner field produces early crowding or positional problems that scramble the expected race shape
scenarios.body: Interference off the gate or a contested early pace from one of the prominent runners unsettles Havana Blue's rhythm, fragmenting the field and turning the race into a scramble; horses with tactical versatility and strong Ascot-style flat-track form such as Northcliff and Golden Long, who handle 6f Good ground particularly well, could pick up the pieces

watchPoints.text: Havana Blue and Golden Long — if Golden Long breaks sharply and contests the lead with Havana Blue rather than settling, it will inject pace that transforms the race shape entirely and opens up for late closers

The 15-runner field increases the risk of early crowding off the rail, particularly for the five redistributed hold-up horses (Diligently, Sword, Saint Lawrence, Fifty Nifty, Northcliff) who are already racing out of their ideal position — any traffic will eliminate their chances

American Gulf's 338-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the field; if he returns to something close to his pre-layoff form he could outrun his odds, but fitness must be assumed compromised until proven otherwise

Golden Long's two consecutive 6f Good-ground wins give him the most directly applicable recent form in the field — watch whether he travels smoothly behind Havana Blue in the early stages, as that will be the clearest signal that he is on a hat-trick
Garfield Shadow's jockey Faleh Bughanaim is unfamiliar at this level — watch for any positional errors off the gate that could cost him the prominent pitch his form profile demands

races.paceDynamic: Gold Star Hero, Cinque Verde, and Rhythm N Hooves are all confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner 5f Ascot handicap on Good ground, which means the pace will be fierce from the gates and is almost certain to be unrelenting throughout. With three horses competing for the lead, none will dictate comfortably — they will burn each other off, compressing the early fractions and leaving nothing in reserve for the final furlong climb. This race shape heavily favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can settle just off the carnage, absorb the pace, and produce their finish as the leaders tie up — profiles like West Acre, Fluorescence, Rocking Ends, and Glamorous Breeze are architecturally best suited. The field contains more prominent types than the race can accommodate at the front, with Dyonisos — a genuine prominent racer — pushed into a midfield mapping because Gold Star Hero, Cinque Verde, and Rhythm N Hooves are most likely to physically secure the early positions; Dyonisos racing out of role tempers its chance materially.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Gold Star Hero, Cinque Verde, and Rhythm N Hooves go hammer-and-tongs from the gates and completely detonate the pace.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners gut each other inside the opening furlong, leaving the prominent-to-midfield trackers in the perfect position to pick up the pieces in the final 100 yards; Ascot's 5f track rewards those who travel sweetly just off a fast pace rather than making it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rails Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types gets a clean split on the inner, tracks the leaders economically, and pounces as the front three falter.
scenarios.body: A prominent horse that avoids the early scrimmage and conserves energy through the first half of the race will have the legs of any surviving front-runner who has taken on rivals; this suits horses with strong recent 5f Good-ground form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: One Leader Pinches It
scenarios.trigger: If Rhythm N Hooves or Cinque Verde gets a clean break, finds a rhythm on a flank, and the others take each other on without troubling it.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic multi-pace scenario one leader occasionally steals a march if rivals' jockeys allow a small gap to open; the winner would need to have found a cleaner passage and carried a manageable weight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so suicidal that even the prominent horses are compromised and the hold-up horses get an unusually clear run through.
scenarios.body: Maelstrom and Mesaafi carry genuine hold-up profiles and have winning form on Good ground at 5f, but this scenario requires both the leaders and the midfield to capitulate, which is unlikely given how many quality prominent types are present; probability is discounted further because Dyonisos — the most prominent redistributed type — is not a genuine hold-up horse.

watchPoints.text: Gold Star Hero, Cinque Verde, and Rhythm N Hooves will all attempt to lead from stall — watch the first furlong for a genuine battle for supremacy that could set an unsustainably fast early tempo and compromise all three well before halfway.

Dyonisos is a naturally prominent racer who is unlikely to secure its preferred early position with three confirmed front-runners in the field — if it is forced to race deep in midfield against its instincts, discount its chance significantly.

Glamorous Breeze has the right profile for this race shape but Gina Mangan's amateur status in a 13-runner competitive handicap introduces a tactical risk, particularly if the field fans wide early and position becomes critical.

Rocking Ends has four wins from 13 runs at 5f on Good ground — the strongest course-and-distance strike rate among the prominent types — and its form figures show it consistently finishes well when a strong pace is set ahead of it; watch for it to travel powerfully at the top of the straight.

Underwriter's fade flag is significant in a race where the pace will test every runner's stamina — if it shows at the front of the hold-up group early in the straight, expect it to empty quickly rather than sustain its effort.
